title: Unit – 4 : Session – 6 : SLO – 2  |  Binary Search Trees — Searching Operation
sections: A Binary Search Tree (BST) is a BINARY TREE with a special property.
All left descendants must be LESS than the node.
All right descendants must be GREATER than the node.
BSTs are used in DATABASE INDEXING and DICTIONARY (lookup/sorting) applications.
In a BST, the left subtree contains nodes SMALLER THAN the root node.
The right subtree contains nodes GREATER THAN the root node.
Search begins at the ROOT node.
If the value to be searched is less than root, go to the LEFT subtree.
If the value to be searched is not found, the result is NULL (NOT FOUND).
II. Algorithm to Search a Value in a BST
